newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares buck trend, set new record high.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares buck trend, set new record high.

text.p: Good liquidity and strong demand for high-technology shares sent the Oslo bourse to new record peaks on Monday, bucking the trend on most major European exchanges. Dealers said the market looked set to gain more as buyers continued to outnumber sellers.
Oslo's Total share index closed at a record 1,102.18 points, a gain of 0.71 percent after hitting an intraday peak at 1,102.56 points. Turnover was 871 million crowns.
"The market's strong partly due to the good liquidity but also because a lot of companies are showing good annual results and meeting expectations," said one broker.
"On a broad basis I see more gains for Oslo."

Telecommunications group Nera was the star performer of the day, climbing 10 crowns, or nearly seven percent, to 348.50 crowns. It also was the most traded share in turnover terms at 54.4 million crowns.
Dealers attributed Nera's popularity to overseas investors.
Conversely, domestic buyers opted for hi-tech group Tandberg, which jumped 21 percent to 85 crowns in 36.5 million crowns of trade.
Food-based conglomerate Orkla, which posted strong 1996 results on Friday, advanced a 13 crowns to end at 550 crowns.
